name: KNE (Kubernetes Network Emulation)
what_it_is: KNE is a containerized network emulation framework built on Kubernetes that allows testing of network control planes using vendor-supplied container images without physical hardware. It provides a standard gRPC interface for topology management and multi-vendor network device emulation.
components: Topology Manager (Kubernetes service with gRPC public API, manages link state and device discovery via CRDs)
Topology Agent (runs per host, enables data plane connectivity between pods)
Network Device Pods (vendor-supplied containers representing emulated network devices)
CLI Tool (manages cluster deployment and topology creation)
measurement: Optical characteristics emulation on data plane wires
Usage metrics reporting (opt-in, disabled by default)
configuration: In-cluster and external service exposure per pod
gRPC topology manager API for programmatic topology management
modes: Topology creation and teardown via CLI
constraints: No native Ethernet device exposure — Linux does not understand associated control messages, requiring the topology agent workaround
Network devices must be vendor-supplied container images; no built-in software router is provided
Requires a running Kubernetes cluster (kind or cloud-based) as a prerequisite
Data plane emulation fidelity is limited by the vendor container implementation, not enforced by KNE itself
docker_services: Vendor-supplied network device containers (e.g., Arista cEOS, Nokia SR Linux, Cisco XRd — vendor-dependent)
Topology Agent container (runs on each Kubernetes node)
notable_absences: No built-in fault injection or traffic impairment primitives
No native traffic generation — requires external tools (e.g., OTG/Ixia-c)
No docker-compose deployment path — Kubernetes is required
No packet capture or flow measurement built into the framework
Measurement and observability depend entirely on vendor container capabilities
